Usage: mcpjam cloud eval run [options]

Start
an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run\nit. The upload-and-launch has a 120s deadline overall,

not per request (raise it
with the global --timeout <ms>); --wait-timeout bounds the RUN instead.

Options:
 --suite <id-or-
name> Eval suite name or ID\n --file <path> Versioned suite file to upload and r
un (.yaml or .json, or - for stdin)\n --project <id-or-name> Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently
updated project)\n --server <id-or-name...> Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only)\n
--environment <id-or-name...> Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one PAID RUN each.\n --cli
ent <id-or-name...> Attached client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several values st
art one PAID RUN each.\n --host <id-or-name...> Deprecated alias for --client. NOT the host-compat catalog id
`mcpjam tools --host` takes.\n --all-targets Run EVERY attached environment (or, if none, every attac
hed host) — one PAID RUN per target\n --iterations <n> Run each case this many times under verdict polic
y 2 (1-10)\n --repetitions <n> Legacy spelling of --iterations\n --case <id-or-title...>
Run only these cases instead of the whole suite\n --exclude-skills Run the 'without skills' arm: no s
kills are pinned, and the run is labelled as excluded\n --refresh-snapshot PERSISTS a new host-config snap
shot on the suite, changing every future run of it. Single-target runs only.\n --notes <text> Free-tex
t note stored on the run\n --min-pass-rate <n> Pass threshold for this run (0-100)\n --match-options <json
> Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. '{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'\n --idempotency-key <key>
Retry key for a lost launch response; for --file, one is minted and printed when omitted\n --wait
Wait for every started run to reach a terminal status\n --wait-timeout <ms> Maximum time to
wait for completion (default 600000; a run held for its judge gets up to 31 more minutes unless this flag is set)\n --reporter <j
son-summary|junit-xml|html> Render the completed run report to stdout\n --out <path> Atomically wri
te the completed report selected by --reporter (default: json-summary)\n --compose-client <id-or-name> Compose a stac
k to run instead of naming a saved environment: the client it runs as. Default is EPHEMERAL (does not attach to the suite).\n --c
ompose-host <id-or-name> Deprecated alias for --compose-client\n --compose-computer <id-or-name> Sandbox
image to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-model <id...> Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces th
e client default unless --with-client-default is set.\n --compose-model-selection <json...> A whole saved model selection (
source, connection, settings.reasoningEffort) as JSON (or @file, or -): one cell for its model, at its effort. Alongside --compose
-model. Repeat it to add several selections for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each distinct selection is its own cell.\n
--with-client-default Also launch an inherit cell that uses each client's pinned model, alongside --compose-mo
del\n --save-targets Attach the composed environments to the suite (append, capped at 10). Default is
ephemeral.\n --compose-server <id-or-name...> Server(s) to pin on the composed stack. Snapshots them into a server group
, so the run keeps testing these servers even if the host's own server list changes later. Mutually exclusive with --compose-serve
r-group.\n --compose-server-group <id> Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-host-serve
rs No longer supported: eval runs take their servers from a server group. Use --compose-server or --compose-ser
ver-group.\n --compose-skill <id...> Project-shared skill IDs to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-secret
<id...> Project SECRET IDs the composed stack grants to its runs. Without one a composed stack carries no credent
